title: iEEG during direct electrical stimulation of orbitofrontal and other sites (Rao, Sellers et al., 2018): continuous-stimulation and single-pulse recordings
description: Intracranial EEG (ECoG grids/strips and depth/stereo-EEG electrodes) from 17 adults undergoing inpatient seizure-localization monitoring. Recordings were made before, during and after continuous 100 Hz direct electrical stimulation of lateral orbitofrontal cortex and other sites, and during single-pulse electrical stimulation. The associated study found that unilateral lateral OFC stimulation acutely improved mood in participants with moderate-to-severe baseline depression symptoms and suppressed low-frequency OFC power. The data are converted to iEEG-BIDS from the original Dryad release.
methods_description: Recordings used Natus clinical, Tucker-Davis Technologies, or Alpha Omega NeuroOmega systems at 1-25 kHz. Continuous stimulation was delivered as bipolar biphasic constant-current trains (1 or 6 mA, 100 Hz, 100 us pulse width, 100-200 s) with a sham block, while mood was assessed with the tablet-based Immediate Mood Scaler. Single-pulse stimulation used 10 mA, 1 Hz, 500 us pulses for 20 s.
